newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank rejects all bids in rev repo tender.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank rejects all bids in rev repo tender.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Wednesday it had rejected all bids, a total of 450 million crowns, at its seven-day securities reverse repurchase tender.

"We have rejected all bids because banks' bids were too high from our point of view...though the interbank money market rates appear to be rising further," Peter Andresic, head of the Open Market Operations Department, told Reuters.
"Such a market anticipation of the long crown position we have been expecting is insufficient, considering our tendency to drain liquidity," Andresic added.
He declined to specify the bids.
Slovak interbank money market rates firmed 10 to 20 basis points in early Wednesday activity, with average offer rates at 20.85 on overnights and 17.89 on six-month money.
Andresic said that a 600 million crown reverse repo contract expired today, and a "bulk" of the past week's foreign liquidity inflow has still been deposited on the market.

However, according to official NBS figures, the banking sector is short of liquidity, with banks' minimum reserve demands fulfilled at 95.65 percent as of Tuesday, after 94.2 percent the previous day.
